R9414.summary: An unnamed Bavarian servant at King John's court writes to Duke Ludwig of Bavaria from Wardein (Nagyvárad): his journey back into Hungary, envoys of the pashas of Belgrade and Bosnia, the Sultan arming 'hundert tausent man' to win Hungary and then turn on Austria, the Ferdinandists taking towns; he asks Ludwig to intercede with Duke Wilhelm, and mentions debts, mining and ore specimens.
R9414.en:
(P1.06-P1.11) [?In the meantime] I have gone back into Hungary; God knows with what great worry the journey came upon
me, and how my gracious prince and lord dispatched me, I leave aside for this time. Almighty God […] has granted me by
His grace that I have come here. Your Princely Grace to …

(P1.33-P2.14) … Your Princely Grace, I send you herewith a copy of the truce made again from Lund, [?…] the orator of
[…] has left, first […] seven weeks ago been sent. In the meantime the Ferdinandists have taken towns […] and several
villages, and likewise made a great plan to surprise […], but fortune has [turned] with […], also he […], as Your
Princely Grace will learn herewith. Gracious lord, these […] have come here: the embassy of the Pasha of Greek
Belgrade and of the Pasha of Bosnia. I have heard their errand [?…]:

system: Homophonic sign alphabet 'G' (own sign set, 42 signs measured), German, with a few word signs (large Ψ, swash X, K) and an unkeyed barred ∂; clear opening, date and address.
